questions.question: If you cannot back your trailer in a straight line, what should you do?

options.text: Swerve back and forth while backing.
Back toward the driver's side.
Back toward the passenger's side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Back toward the driver's side.
questions.explanation: If you cannot back your trailer straight, back it on a curve toward the driver's side. This gives you the best visibility while backing.

questions.question: What happens if anti-lock brakes are on only one axle?

options.text: Will not make a difference in braking.
Will provide increased control in braking.
Will likely cause the air brakes to malfunction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Will provide increased control in braking.
questions.explanation: Even with anti-lock brakes on just one axle, the driver has more braking control than without any anti-lock brakes.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT help prevent a rig from rolling over?

options.text: Keeping the cargo as close to the ground as possible
Driving slowly around turns
Driving on the shoulder of a road

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving on the shoulder of a road
questions.explanation: To prevent a rig from rolling over, keep cargo weight low and drive slowly around turns. Driving on the road shoulder does not help prevent rollovers.

questions.question: When backing your tractor to couple it to a trailer, the trailer brakes should be:

options.text: Deactivated.
Locked.
Unlocked.

questions.correctAnswerText: Locked.
questions.explanation: Before backing your tractor under the trailer during coupling, lock the trailer brakes. This is important for safely coupling combination vehicles.

questions.question: When coupling, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure to couple the proper glad hands.
Only couple one set of glad hands.
It is best to leave one glad hand loose.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure to couple the proper glad hands.
questions.explanation: Connect the correct pairs of glad hands. They are often color-coded: blue for service lines and red for emergency lines. This helps prevent mistakes.

questions.question: After a pre-trip inspection, you should ensure that the:

options.text: Service line valve is closed.
Trailer hand brake is applied.
Emergency line valve is open.

questions.correctAnswerText: Service line valve is closed.
questions.explanation: Before driving, open the rear emergency and service line valves to check for air flow. Then close both valves before you start driving.

questions.question: If a parked trailer has no spring brakes, how should you keep it from moving?

options.text: Park it against a wall or another vehicle.
Use chock blocks.
Park it on a slight incline.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use chock blocks.
questions.explanation: If a parked trailer has no spring brakes, use wheel chocks to prevent it from rolling.

questions.question: Trailers with low underneath clearance have problems when driving over:

options.text: Bridges.
Railroad tracks.
Overpasses.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are hard to cross with trailers that have low clearance. Low-slung units and single-axle tractors pulling long trailers are especially difficult on raised crossings.

questions.question: Why do combination vehicles need extra space on the road?

options.text: They drive more slowly than other commercial vehicles.
They are heavier than other commercial vehicles.
They need more space to turn and stop than other commercial vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They need more space to turn and stop than other commercial vehicles.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles are longer and need more space to turn and stop. Managing space properly is very important when operating combination vehicles.

questions.question: When should you use the trailer hand valve?

options.text: Only when the trailer is carrying a load
Only to test the trailer's brakes
Only in inclement weather when the trailer may skid

questions.correctAnswerText: Only to test the trailer's brakes
questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve (also called a trolley valve or Johnson bar) controls the trailer brakes. Use it only to test the brakes. Using it while driving can cause a skid.

questions.question: What happens if the emergency air line loses pressure?

options.text: The Anti-Lock Braking System will turn on.
The service air line will turn on.
The emergency brakes will turn on.

questions.correctAnswerText: The emergency brakes will turn on.
questions.explanation: The emergency air line controls the emergency brakes on a combination vehicle. If the emergency line loses air pressure, the emergency trailer brakes will turn on.

questions.question: What happens if the emergency air line loses pressure?

options.text: The service brakes will turn on.
The tractor protection valve will close.
The rear trailer will separate from the tractor.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tractor protection valve will close.
questions.explanation: The tractor protection valve keeps air in the trailer's brakes if the trailer breaks away or leaks. When the emergency line loses air pressure, the tractor protection valve closes and the emergency trailer brakes turn on.

questions.question: In a vehicle with an automatic tractor protection valve, the valve will pop out when air pressure drops to what level?

options.text: 20 to 45 psi
75 to 105 psi
50 to 65 psi

questions.correctAnswerText: 20 to 45 psi
questions.explanation: In vehicles with an automatic tractor protection valve, the valve pops out when air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi. When it pops out, the protection valve closes and stops air from flowing.

questions.question: What is one benefit of keeping cargo low?

options.text: It prevents rollovers.
It lets you drive faster.
It makes turns safer.

questions.correctAnswerText: It prevents rollovers.
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when you turn too quickly with a combination vehicle. To prevent rollovers, keep the center of gravity low by loading cargo as close to the ground as possible.

questions.question: When should you look into the back of the fifth wheel?

options.text: While testing your air brakes
If your vehicle begins to skid
When inspecting a coupling

questions.correctAnswerText: When inspecting a coupling
questions.explanation: When inspecting a coupling, go under the trailer and look into the back of the fifth wheel. Check that the fifth wheel jaws are locked around the kingpin shank.

questions.question: How should a driver test the tractor protection valve?

options.text: Pull the yellow, diamond-shaped knob.
Release air by pressing the brake pedal.
Unlock the trailer doors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release air by pressing the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Test the tractor protection valve by letting the air supply charge fully, turning off the engine, then releasing air by pressing the brake pedal several times. The valve should move to its emergency position when air pressure drops to an unsafe level.

questions.question: What do shut-off valves do?

options.text: Stop air from escaping the brake system.
Stop air from entering the brake system.
Control out-of-control vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop air from escaping the brake system.
questions.explanation: Shut-off valves control air flow between trailers in the air supply lines. The rear shut-off valve should always stay closed to keep air from leaving the brake system.

questions.question: What happens if an air supply control is in its "emergency" position?

options.text: The vehicle will speed up.
The trailer emergency brakes will turn on.
The air supply to the trailer will increase.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer emergency brakes will turn on.
questions.explanation: Older vehicles may have lever-operated tractor protection controls instead of knobs. When an air supply control is in the "emergency" position, the air supply stops and the trailer emergency brakes turn on.

questions.question: When coupling, what should you do?

options.text: Assume all vehicles are the same.
Make sure you are coupling correctly.
Accept cracks in the mounting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure you are coupling correctly.
questions.explanation: Incorrect coupling or uncoupling of combination vehicles can be very dangerous.

questions.question: During a trip, which valve should be open?

options.text: Rear service line shut-off valve
Rear supply line shut-off valve
Inner shut-off valves

questions.correctAnswerText: Inner shut-off valves
questions.explanation: At the start of a trip, make sure all shut-off valves are open except for the last valves on the rear trailer. This ensures air reaches all trailer brakes and does not escape from the back of the vehicle.
